title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page. L is a totally ordered set. M = M_0 ⊔ M_1, where M_0 = L (the 'points') and M_1 is the set of bounded intervals I_{ab} with a<b (the 'edges'). Two structures sit on M. The first is an order-type relation ≤ ('lies to the left of / precedes'). The second is an incidence relation ⊴ (a ⊴ I_{ab} when a is an endpoint), with boundary δX (δI_{ab} = {a,b}). The previous page proved that two distinct elements X, Y are '≤-comparable in the sense ≸' iff they are 'disjoint/adjacent' (X|·|Y). Its corollary: a subset is a parfigure iff it is totally ordered by ≤.

This page first fixes conventions. 'Figure' means finite figure, i.e. one works in the atelier F ⊂ 𝔓(M) of finite figures. Two descriptions follow:
- Prefig(M) = Dreg*(M,≤): the prefigures are the ≤-chains.
- Fig(M) = Dreg*(M,≤) ∩ 𝔓f(M,⊴): the figures are the finite subsets of M that are totally ordered by ≤ and closed under ⊴ (they contain the endpoints of their intervals).

Geometrically, a figure is a finite 'polygon' (a 1-dimensional cell configuration) on the line L: finitely many points and segments, ordered left to right and closed under taking boundaries.

Grothendieck then wants a 'complementary prefigure' Φ' for each prefigure Φ, for use in studying complementarity relations. The complement of a finite configuration on a line has unbounded components. So if L lacks a minimum or maximum, one must leave M and adjoin 'infinite intervals' I_{<a} and I_{>a}. Even when L has extremes ω_0 and ω_1, adjoining these intervals makes the formulas cleaner. With them, δΦ' ⊂ δΦ, and the next page states δΦ' = δΦ. Without them one only gets δΦ' ⊂ δΦ ∪ {ω_0, ω_1}, and the extremal points η must be distributed: η = (Φ∩η) ⊔ (Φ'∩η), each extremity going to exactly one of Φ, Φ'.

The next page formalizes this as M̂ = M̂_0 ⊔ M̂_1 with M̂_1 = M_1 ⊔ M_1^- ⊔ M_1^+. These are formal symbols with ∂I_{<a} = {a}, |I_{<a}| = L_{≤a}, and interior L_{<a}.

Purpose: a purely combinatorial, order-theoretic model of 1-dimensional 'tame' figures and their Boolean/complementation calculus. It is a toy case of a general theory of 'ateliers' (families of figures closed under operations), presumably meant to generalize to higher-dimensional combinatorial cell structures.
errors: Minor inconsistency, not a real error: this page asserts δΦ' ⊂ δΦ, while the next page states δΦ = δΦ'. The equality holds for the symmetric complementation with infinite intervals; the inclusion is the weaker form written first.
The parenthetical on η (the extremities of L) is cut off and incomplete on this page. The exact condition on which of the two prefigures receives each extremal point is not fully stated here.

ideas.what: Figures in a totally ordered set as finite subsets of points-plus-intervals that are ≤-chains closed under the boundary/incidence relation ⊴
ideas.modern_name: finite 1-dimensional cell complexes on a linear order; 1-dimensional definable sets / cell decompositions (o-minimal cell decomposition in dim 1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: cell decomposition: Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight, van den Dries (1984–86); combinatorially folklore
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this combinatorial 'atelier' formalism is unpublished

ideas.what: Complementary prefigure obtained by adjoining formal unbounded intervals I_{<a}, I_{>a}, so that complementation becomes boundary-preserving (δΦ' = δΦ) even when L has endpoints
ideas.modern_name: complement in the Boolean algebra of finite unions of points and intervals; compactification / adding rays at infinity

ideas.what: 'Atelier' F ⊂ 𝔓(M) as an ambient family of admissible figures
ideas.modern_name: a class of 'tame' subsets, roughly analogous to a structure/Boolean algebra of definable sets
ideas.where_published: possibly echoed in 'La Longue Marche' / Esquisse discussions of tame topology; unsure

missed.claim: This is Grothendieck developing, in 1986, a purely order-combinatorial calculus of 1-dimensional 'figures' with complementation, closely parallel to the 1-dimensional case of o-minimal cell decomposition. That theory was being developed contemporaneously by model theorists. The link between his 'ateliers' and o-minimality/tame topology is implicit, not stated on this page.
missed.quote: Les figures sont les parties finies de M, tot. ordonnées par ≤, et fermées pour ⊴.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historians tracing Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' programme may find here a concrete, unpublished combinatorial starting point. Mathematically the 1-dim content is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is elementary: points and intervals on a line, plus complements via unbounded rays. Its interest is historical. It shows the concrete combinatorial form of Grothendieck's 1986 'ateliers' project, plausibly related to tame topology, but there is no unexpected result.
transcription_corrections: 'bien ordonnées par ≤' should read 'tot[alement] ordonnées par ≤' (the image shows 'Lot./tot. ordonnées'); this is consistent with the corollary on the previous page.
'en nous faisant introduire des "intervalles infinis"' likely reads 'en nous faisant intervenir des "intervalles infinis"'.
'rapports contrôlables' is uncertain; it could be 'rapports combinatoires' or a similar word.
'(extr. de 𝓛)' means extremities of L, i.e. its smallest and largest elements ω_0, ω_1.
